collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 9-12 and an adult; in the story (name1) is very tall for (his/her) age)

collection.description: A ten-year-old as tall as an adult was snapped at to act their age: tell the adult how old they are, or tell someone else.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) is ten, and already as tall as most adults. People keep forgetting how young (subject.he/she) is. Today (friend) asked (subject.him/her) to carry a heavy load to the gardens, then snapped at (subject.him/her) for dawdling and for playing with a frog on the way. "Act your age," (friend) said. (subject) is sitting on a rock, stung.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) marches back and says, "I'm TEN." (friend) stops. "...Ten?" (friend.He/she) had genuinely thought (subject) was much older. (friend.He/she) sits down beside (subject.him/her). "I'm sorry. I was acting like your size, not your age." (subject) sniffs. "Can I play with the frog?" "You can play with the frog," says (friend).

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (subject) goes and tells (subject.his/her) family, who are not pleased with (friend). They have a word. Later (friend) comes to find (subject) by the stream, where (subject.he/she) is building a frog house. (friend) helps (subject.him/her) build it. (friend.He/she) doesn't say much. At the end (friend.he/she) says, "Ten. I won't forget." (friend.He/she) doesn't.
